Name: COOloop
Description:
COOloop is a London-based deep-tech company developing a proprietary catalyst platform to convert CO2 and green hydrogen directly into ultra-low carbon ethanol.
Our technology is based on a novel metal-organic framework (MOF) derived catalyst, originally developed through PhD and postdoctoral research at Monash University. Unlike biological fermentation routes, our thermochemical process converts CO2 and H2 directly into ethanol.
Using biogenic CO2 and green hydrogen, our process can achieve negative greenhouse gas intensity — providing significant compliance advantages under RFNBO regulations and positioning our ethanol as a structurally differentiated product in mandate-driven fuel markets.
Our target markets:
• Road fuel compliance — EU RED III and the German Quoten system
• Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) via the Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) pathway
• Industrial solvents and pharma-grade ethanol
Where we are:
Currently at TRL 4–5, with demonstrated catalyst stability across multiple batch cycles and ethanol production from CO2 and H2 confirmed in the lab. We are progressing to continuous flow process testing, the critical step toward pilot scale and filing IP to protect our ethanol production route.
We are in active discussion with several large industry players on technical collaboration, scale-up and commercial partnership.
COOloop was incorporated in August 2025 and is currently raising its pre-seed round.

Name: BLUSENS
Description:
Blusens is an electronics and IoT engineering practice founded in 2014, designing complete IoT systems from first principles — where hardware, RF, connectivity, backend and user-facing software are built as one coherent stack rather than separate parts assembled together.
In 2015, before standardised residential IoT platforms existed, Blusens designed an original end-to-end architecture combining local sub-GHz RF communication, dual-mode cellular and WiFi backhaul, server-side time-series data storage, and monitoring visualisation built for non-technical users. The same architectural model went on to underpin two separate climate-tech products in the Sustainable Ventures ecosystem — two different problems solved by one design.
That architecture was carried through to completion: UKCA certification across multiple product lines, and production scaled past 30,000 units in the field. The original 2015 roadmap — which identified EMC certification and volume manufacturing as the milestones separating a prototype from a deployable product — was seen through end to end.
Blusens represents a decade of owning product development across the full stack: multi-radio IoT platform design, RF and EMC regulatory compliance, PCB design, non-isolated power supply design, and the manufacturing engineering required to take climate-tech hardware from prototype to volume.

Name: Carbon Lock Solutions
Description:
We aim to unlock the capacity of oceans to make carbon dioxide removal (CDR) efficient, durable and scalable, using innovative tech that tweaks conditions favourable for CO2 drawdown and lockdown.

As atmospheric CO2 pass levels 1.5X higher than the pre-industrial mean and global warming is expected to pass the Paris Agreement target of +1.5 oC in just 5 years, the need for accelerating CDR is never more pressing. 

Our oceans are the biggest buffer to excess warming absorbing over 30% of CO2 emssions and over 90% of excess heat. But its reaching saturation and dissolved CO2 is increasing ocean acidity. Heat and acidification is now threatening marine ecosystems as the smallest, carbonate organisms, struggle against dissolution of their protective "shells".

The IPCC indicate CDR at 8-10 Gigatonnes (Gt) per annum will be required in all pathways to net zero by 2050. While aforestation accounts for 2 Gt/yr, upto 60% of the remaining gap is expected to be filled by novel solutions.

The Carbon Lock Project aims to develop innovative CDR technoligies that removes atmospheric carbon dioxide, restores ocean alkalinity, and revalues natural and engineered solutions where synergies can bring value and efficiencies to climate resortation.

Name: Rockit Tech
Description:
The “Rockit” technology from Heriot-Watt University prevents undesired leaks of greenhouse gases (methane, CO2), flammables, toxins, carcinogens (hydrocarbon gas, H2S, mercury vapour), and stored gases (hydrogen, CO2) from escaping through drilled wells to the atmosphere. 

It seals potential leak paths and fractures around the borehole of a well within the rock itself with an impermeable mineral barrier that is resistant to aggressive acidic conditions downhole. No flow from surrounding rock formation to the wellbore is possible, cement plugs are protected from degradation and therefore fluids (gases, oil, contaminated water) are locked deep underground for many thousands of years.

Name: Olivine Technologies
Description:
At Olivine Technologies, we are at the forefront of developing innovative carbon storage solutions, specifically tailored for the spirits and ethanol sectors. 
Our cutting-edge reactor technology utilizes olivine, a naturally occurring mineral, to effectively capture and store biogenic CO2 produced during fermentation processes. This approach not only helps distilleries reduce their carbon footprint but also enhances their sustainability credentials in an increasingly climate-conscious market.

Our Approach to Carbon Storage
1. Advanced Reactor Technology:
Our primary focus is on advancing reactor technology that leverages olivine’s unique properties. Olivine reacts with CO2 to form stable carbonates, providing a permanent and environmentally friendly solution for permanent low cost carbon storage. This method is both cost-effective and efficient, making it an attractive option for distilleries looking to offset their emissions.

2. Biogenic CO2 Capture:
During the fermentation process, significant amounts of biogenic CO2 are produced. Unlike fossil fuel-derived CO2, biogenic CO2 is part of the natural carbon cycle. By capturing this CO2, our technology helps distilleries achieve negative emissions, effectively removing carbon from the atmosphere.

3. Enhancing Brand Sustainability:
Consumers and regulators are increasingly concerned about the environmental impact of the products they purchase. Our solution allows distilleries to market their products as carbon-neutral. This can provide a competitive edge in a future market characterized by heightened climate sensitivity.

4. Addressing Scope 3 Emissions:
While many distilleries have made progress in reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions, Scope 3 emissions remain a significant challenge. Our technology provides a viable pathway for distilleries to address these indirect emissions, aligning with broader sustainability goals and commitments, such as achieving Net Zero.

Name: AET Flexible Space
Description:
AET Flexible Space has been redefining how buildings breathe since 1993. What began as a family business and one of the main global distributors of the pioneering Hiross Flexible Space system — originally designed to cool data centres in Asia — has evolved into a UK manufacturing success story, leading the future of intelligent, sustainable climate control.

AET’s UfAC system utilises the void beneath a raised floor as a plenum to supply conditioned air via modular floor-recessed FantileTM units. Air is then drawn back through either floor- or ceiling-level returns to the central CAMTM unit, filtered, mixed with fresh air, and recirculated. The result is a self-contained, adaptable, and energy-efficient system that eliminates the need for ceiling ductwork, offering unparalleled flexibility and comfort.

Beyond performance, sustainability is built into every component. By removing bulky ductwork and overhead services, AET systems reduce materials, installation time, and embodied carbon, delivering up to 18% less Upfront Carbon and 16% lower Whole-Life Embodied Carbon than conventional HVAC systems. In operation, energy savings reach up to 52% for refrigerant-based and 19% for water-based systems, directly supporting carbon reduction targets and green building certifications.

AET’s Flexible Space systems help developers and occupiers create adaptable, future-proof workspaces that evolve with their needs. Reduced floor-to-floor heights optimise structure and cost — saving up to £1.7 million in a typical 10-storey scheme — while installation and reconfiguration can be completed swiftly, with minimal downtime.

From the world’s first 70-storey installation in Hong Kong’s The Centre to London’s most forward-thinking refurbishments, AET continues to deliver spaces that are better for people, better for buildings, and better for the planet, redefining how we design, condition, and experience the modern workspace.

Name: UAP | Atmospheric Processing
Description:
UAP is developing the world’s first non-cryogenic atmospheric refinery.

We’re building a parallel route to noble gas supply — extracting neon, krypton, and xenon directly from air using a patented plasma separation process. Our technology is designed to operate alongside existing cryogenic infrastructure, addressing the structural supply gap that conventional air separation cannot close on its own.

Noble gases are critical to semiconductor manufacturing, space propulsion, fusion energy, and medical imaging. Demand is growing. Supply is constrained. The industry needs additional capacity from a fundamentally different architecture.

Our technology is supported by a US patent grant, a co-development partnership with CERN, and engineering validation with Amentum. 

Our business model is built around gas supply, not hardware sales. CO2 is recovered as a by-product. Clean air is returned.

We’re building an industrial infrastructure company that also decarbonises — not the other way around.

Description:
Welcome to Retyre Limited - Revolutionizing Tyre Recycling

At Retyre, we're driving the future of sustainable tyre recycling with our groundbreaking Fluid Dynamic Pulverisation Technology (FDPTTM). Founded on a decade and a half of dedicated research and developed in collaboration with Imperial College London, Retyre is on a mission to transform tyre waste into resources. Our patented technology not only addresses the critical issue of tyre disposal but also sets a new standard for environmental responsibility in the industry.

Our Vision:
To lead the global shift towards sustainable tyre recycling, ensuring that every tyre is recycled and repurposed, contributing to a circular economy, and eliminating the environmental impact of tyre waste.

Our Innovation:
FDPTTM represents a leap forward in recycling technology, using ultra-high-pressure water jets to break down tyres into their constituent materials. This process produces Activ-RTM, a premium, sustainable rubber powder that is reintroduced into the supply chain, reducing the demand for virgin materials and contributing to a more sustainable world.

Our Impact:
With strategic partnerships, including a significant collaboration with Siemens, Retyre is poised for global expansion. Our ambitious goal to deploy 5,000 machines worldwide in the next five years underscores our commitment to making a tangible environmental impact. Through innovation, we aim to not only revolutionize tyre recycling but also inspire a generation of businesses to prioritize sustainability in their operations.

Join Us:
Retyre is more than a company; it’s a movement. As we expand our reach and refine our technology, we invite you to join us on this journey. Whether you’re a potential partner, investor, or someone passionate about sustainability, follow our page for updates on our progress, insights into our technology, and stories of impact from around the world.
